summary: Circlestone Labs' fine-tuning advice (a rank 32 LoRA at 2e-5, the LLM adapter left alone) and ComfyUI's Anima template sampling (Euler, 30 steps, CFG 4, with its negative prompt).

sources.label: Anima model card: Finetuning Tips (Circlestone Labs)
NVIDIA's Cosmos Predict2 text-to-image LoRA defaults (cosmos_predict2/models/text2image_model.py)

samples.negative: worst quality, low quality, score_1, score_2, score_3, blurry, jpeg artifacts, sepia

notes: The makers: don't train the LLM adapter, which shapes the text before the model sees it and is easy to degrade. ZenTrainer never adapts it.
The makers: a light touch. It's a base model with no aesthetic tuning to fight, and it knows a great many concepts already: start at 2e-5 for rank 32 and move up or down from there.
Keep a negative prompt: at CFG 4 an empty one draws streaks of noise, before any training (the base model in plain ComfyUI does the same).
An anime model: prompts in its own style ("1girl, solo, long silver hair, ...") come out cleanest; photo prompts drift.
A trigger that's a real word is read as one ("aurora" draws the northern lights): a made-up word trains cleaner.
Shift 3 is ComfyUI's default for Anima already.
ZenTrainer's LoRA on Anima trains the layers NVIDIA's Cosmos Predict2 LoRA does: each block's attention q/k/v/output and its two MLP layers. The AdaLN modulation and Anima's text adapter stay frozen.
